analysis.investment_thesis: KSB is a quality industrial compounder with pristine balance sheet and expanding margins, benefiting from India's water infrastructure and energy transition tailwinds — but revenue CAGR of 14% and a sharp deceleration to 6.5% in FY25 fall well short of Fisher's 20-30% growth threshold. At 58x P/E, the market is pricing in exceptional growth that the numbers do not yet support.
key_strengths: Near-zero debt (D/E = 0.00, borrowings only INR 5 Cr) with INR 1,644 Cr reserves — fortress balance sheet funds growth without dilution
ROCE of 24.5% and expanding operating margins (INR 106 Cr EBIT in 2016 → INR 374 Cr in 2025 at 15% CAGR) signal genuine pricing power in specialty pumps/valves
Secular demand drivers — water infra, wastewater, decarbonization, mining — give KSB multi-decade runway with backing of German parent KSB SE's global technology
key_risks: Growth deceleration is real: revenue grew only 6.5% in FY25 (INR 2,533→2,696 Cr) vs. a 9-yr CAGR of 14%, signalling possible demand softness or order-cycle troughs
Valuation demands perfection — 58x P/E and 44x EV/EBITDA for a 14% revenue grower leaves no margin of safety if growth disappoints further
FCF collapsed to zero in FY25 (OCF INR 93 Cr minus capex INR 94 Cr); while capex signals expansion, sustained zero/negative FCF limits compounding power
red_flags: Revenue growth deceleration to 6.5% in FY25 — well below the historical 14% CAGR and Fisher's 20%+ threshold
No R&D expenditure data available; as a foreign parent subsidiary, innovation pipeline depends on KSB SE rather than indigenous R&D — a concern for long-term competitive moat
ROE at 18.3% is below Fisher's 20% benchmark and has not meaningfully expanded despite profitability improvement
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my scuttlebutt lens, KSB is an admirable industrial business — specialty pumps and valves serving critical infrastructure (water, wastewater, energy, decarbonization) where switching costs are high and technical reputation matters enormously. The 9-year operating profit CAGR of 15% with zero leverage and gross margins of 46% tell me the product is genuinely differentiated. Management has been disciplined: borrowings went from INR 62 Cr in 2020 to just INR 5 Cr in 2025, while reserves compounded from INR 856 Cr to INR 1,644 Cr. The rising CWIP (INR 25 Cr → INR 89 Cr) suggests capacity investment that could fuel the next leg of growth — a positive signal if demand materialises.

However, I cannot call this a Fisher-grade exceptional compounder at current prices. Revenue growth of just 6.5% in FY25 is a flashing warning — my 15-point checklist demands companies that can sustain 20%+ sales growth for years. The fact that this is principally a subsidiary of a German parent (KSB SE, 69.8% promoter) limits my confidence in indigenous management depth and independent R&D ambition. Most critically, paying 58x earnings for a business growing earnings at ~16% implies a PEG ratio above 3.5x — far from the "growth at a reasonable price" zone even by generous standards. I would revisit aggressively on a meaningful correction to sub-35x P/E, where the quality would genuinely shine.
